tldr: This thread pairs an Oct 18 research item on LLM inference over mixed hardware with DeepSeek's Oct 20 DeepInfer release. Only the DeepInfer coverage is one story; the first item shares words, not an event.
whats_new: DeepSeek open-sourced DeepInfer on Oct 20, the inference framework behind its production services; The Information (Oct 21) ties it to the company's high-margin inference.
why_it_matters: DeepInfer is the serving stack DeepSeek runs in production, so its scheduling and memory choices are a reference for anyone self-hosting large open-weight models, not a research demo.

status.detail: DeepInfer is public; no independent benchmark or adoption report is in this thread yet.

beats.headline: Mixed-hardware co-design paper shares the inference topic only
DeepSeek open-sources DeepInfer, its production inference framework
beats.summary: SiliconANGLE reports the release Oct 20; The Information follows Oct 21 on the margins it supports.

open_questions: Do independent benchmarks reproduce DeepSeek's claimed inference cost advantage on non-DeepSeek hardware?
Does DeepInfer run outside DeepSeek's own model architectures?
take_for_builders: Read the DeepInfer repo's supported-hardware and model lists before planning a migration from vLLM or SGLang; wait for an independent throughput comparison on your own GPUs.
